message.content:
Here are some practical, everyday tips to keep your piano sounding and looking its best: | # | Tip | Why it matters | How to do it | |---|-----|----------------|--------------| | 1 | **Control Humidity** | Pianos are sensitive to moisture. Too dry and the wood shrinks; too wet and it swells or warps. | • Keep the piano in a room with 45‑55 % relative humidity.
• Use a hygrometer to monitor levels.
• In winter, use a humidifier; in summer, a dehumidifier or silica gel packs. | | 2 | **Regular Tuning** | Even a well‑maintained piano will drift out of tune over time. | • Tune at least twice a year (or more if you play often).
• Use a professional tuner for accurate pitch and temperament. | | 3 | **Daily Light Cleaning** | Dust and fingerprints dull the finish and can damage the keys. | • Wipe keys with a soft, dry microfiber cloth.
• For sticky spots, use a mild soap solution (water + a drop of dish soap) and a damp cloth—never soak the keys. | | 4 | **Keep It Out of Direct Sunlight** | UV rays fade the finish and can warp the wood. | • Position the piano away from windows or use UV‑blocking curtains. | | 5 | **Avoid Extreme Temperature Changes** | Rapid shifts can cause the wood to expand/contract unevenly. | • Keep the piano in a room with stable temperature (ideally 18–22 °C / 65–72 °F). | | 6 | **Use a Piano Cover When Not in Use** | Protects from dust, pets, and accidental spills. | • Choose a breathable, non‑adhesive cover. | | 7 | **Check the Pedals** | Loose or stiff pedals affect playability. | • Inspect for wobble or resistance; tighten screws or replace worn parts. | | 8 | **Inspect the Strings and Hammers** | Over time, strings can stretch or hammers can wear. | • Have a technician check for broken or loose strings and replace worn hammers. | | 9 | **Avoid Heavy Objects on the Piano** | The frame and soundboard can crack under weight. | • Never place books, boxes, or furniture on top of the piano. | | 10 | **Professional Servicing** | A full service includes voicing, regulation, and a thorough inspection. | • Schedule a comprehensive check every 3–5 years, depending on usage. | | 11 | **Use a Piano Stand or Ledge** | If you need to move the piano, use a proper stand to avoid scratches or dents. | • Never slide the piano on bare floor; use padded rollers or a dolly. | | 12 | **Keep the Piano Away from Pets** | Cats and dogs can scratch keys or chew on cords. | • Use cord covers and keep pets at a safe distance. | | 13 | **Mind the Water** | Even a small spill can damage the soundboard. | • Clean up any liquid immediately with a dry cloth; if water gets inside, call a technician. | | 14 | **Play Regularly** | A piano that sits idle can develop “dead spots” where the soundboard has become stiff. | • Even light practice keeps the action and soundboard in good condition. | ### Quick Checklist (Monthly) 1. **Check humidity** – adjust if outside 45‑55 %. 2. **Clean keys** – wipe with a dry cloth. 3. **Inspect pedals** – ensure smooth movement. 4. **Look for cracks or loose parts** – note any issues for a technician. ### When to Call a Technician - **Tuning** (every 6–12 months). - **Voicing** (every 3–5 years). - **Regulation** (every 5–7 years). - **Soundboard repairs** (if you hear a “dead” tone or notice cracks). - **Any visible damage** (cracks, warped wood, loose strings). By following these simple habits, you’ll preserve the piano’s tone, extend its life, and keep it ready for your next performance. Happy playing!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are some tips to maintain a piano?" They want general maintenance tips. We can provide a list: humidity control, tuning, cleaning, etc. No function call needed.
